name: Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination
department: Ministry of Home Affairs (BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, SSB)
summary: Direct entry as Assistant Commandant, a Group A officer, in the BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP and SSB. There are four stages: two written papers, physical standards and efficiency tests, an interview, and a medical. Open to graduate men and women aged 20 to 25.

status.note: Held every year. Usual pattern: notification in February, written exam in July or August, then physical tests, interviews and medicals over the following months.

posts.name: Assistant Commandant, Border Security Force
posts.responsibilities: Guarding the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders.

posts.name: Assistant Commandant, Central Reserve Police Force
posts.responsibilities: Internal security, counter-insurgency, law and order support.

posts.name: Assistant Commandant, Central Industrial Security Force
posts.responsibilities: Security of airports, ports, PSUs and critical installations.

posts.name: Assistant Commandant, Sashastra Seema Bal
posts.responsibilities: Guarding the Nepal and Bhutan borders.

posts.name: Assistant Commandant, Indo-Tibetan Border Police
posts.responsibilities: Guarding the China border in high-altitude areas.

age.summary: At least 20 and under 25 on 1 August of the exam year. For 2026: born between 2 August 2001 and 1 August 2006.

relaxations.category: Civilian central government servants and ex-servicemen
relaxations.note: Total relaxation for government service is capped at 5 years.

education.summary: A bachelor's degree in any subject from a recognised university, or equivalent.

eligibility.physical: Men: height 165 cm, chest 81 cm unexpanded with 5 cm expansion, weight 50 kg. Women: height 157 cm, weight 46 kg. Physical Efficiency Test (men / women): 100 m in 16 / 18 seconds; 800 m in 3 min 45 s / 4 min 45 s; long jump 3.5 m / 3.0 m (3 chances); shot put 7.26 kg, 4.5 m (men only, 3 chances). Standard heights are relaxable for some categories as per Appendix V.
eligibility.medical: Medical Standards Test after the interview, as per Appendix V; appeals are allowed only against the medical result.
other: Women found pregnant at the PST/PET stage have their appointment kept in abeyance until after confinement, subject to fitness.
PET is qualifying: failing it means no interview call.
eligibility.examVsPost: You list force preferences. Allocation depends on rank, category, preference and medical fitness. Not all forces post women in every role.
disqualifications: Height or chest even 0.1 cm below the minimum disqualifies.
eligibility.reservation: Central reservation applies (SC, ST, OBC, EWS). 10% of total vacancies are earmarked for ex-servicemen.

eligibilityRules.notes: Under 25 on 1 Aug 2026 (up to 24 completed years). Physical standards and PET apply. Not open to PwBD candidates (field posts).

stages.name: Written exam

papers.name: Paper I: General Ability and Intelligence (objective)
Paper II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension (descriptive)
papers.notes: Part A essays 80 marks (English or Hindi); Part B comprehension, precis and language skills 120 marks (English only). Evaluated only if you clear the minimum in Paper I.

stages.notes: Minimum qualifying marks are fixed separately for each paper.

stages.name: Physical Standards and Physical Efficiency Tests

selection.meritCalculation: Final merit = written (450) + interview (150) = 600. NCC certificate holders get consideration at the interview.
selection.languages: Paper I in English and Hindi; Paper II essay in English or Hindi, the rest in English only.
selection.documentVerification: Proof of degree is required after qualifying for the physical tests.
selection.probation: Basic training at the force academy, then probation as per force rules.

sections.subject: Paper I: General Ability and Intelligence
topics: General mental ability: logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, numerical ability, data interpretation
General science, including IT, biotechnology and environmental science
Current events: culture, music, arts, literature, sports, governance, society, development, business, international relations
Indian polity and economy, public administration, security issues, human rights
History of India, growth of nationalism and the freedom movement

sections.subject: Paper II: General Studies, Essay and Comprehension
topics: Part A (80 marks): essays on modern Indian history and the freedom struggle, geography, polity, economy, security and human rights, analytical ability
Part B (120 marks): comprehension, precis writing, counter-arguments, grammar and language skills (English)

supplementary: Physical training for the PET should start alongside written preparation.

rankAndAllocation.text: Candidates are allotted forces by rank, category and preference, subject to medical fitness and vacancies in each force.

specialAllowances.name: Risk and hardship allowances
specialAllowances.detail: Paid by area of posting (border, high altitude, counter-insurgency).

salary.pension: National Pension System (CAPF personnel joining after 1 Jan 2004).
salary.notes: CAPFs are central civil forces, so civilian central pay rules apply, with force-specific allowances.

career.promotionNotes: Promotions depend on vacancies, service records and courses. Many top posts (IG, ADG, DG) are also filled by IPS officers on deputation, which limits cadre officers' rise; this is a long-running grievance in the forces.
career.macp: Group A: time-scale and non-functional upgradation per rules.

benefits.detail: Force accommodation and CAPF medical facilities.

workLife.postings: Borders, conflict zones, high altitude (ITBP), industrial and airport sites (CISF).
workLife.transfers: Frequent rotation between hard and peace postings.
workLife.workload: Very demanding; long periods away from family.
workLife.hazards: High: insurgency, border firing, terrain and weather.

difficulty.rationale: A general syllabus plus a descriptive paper, a qualifying physical test and an interview, for about 300 to 350 posts a year. Official applicant counts were not checked, so competition is rated qualitatively.

ratings.rationale: Annual exam; promotions above Commandant are slower because of IPS deputation to senior posts.

factors.note: Failing the PET or medical ends selection.
Border and insurgency areas are part of normal service.

sections.title: The four stages
paragraphs: Two written papers (450 marks), a qualifying physical test, an interview (150 marks) and a medical. Paper II is checked only if you clear the cut in Paper I, so the objective paper is your first gate.

sections.title: Common confusions
bullets: CAPF AC is not IPS; it is the cadre officer entry of each force.
Paper II is descriptive and partly English-only, which many candidates underestimate.
Even 0.1 cm below the height or chest minimum disqualifies.

gaps: Official applicant and selection counts and cutoffs not collected.
dataQuality.notes: Vacancies, eligibility, scheme and physical standards from the 2026 notification.
